pure-announcement.rationale: Despite promotional framing it is an architecture deep-dive whose universal-AST and incremental-indexing techniques transfer beyond CodePrism, not a launch or release note.

duplicate.rationale: code-knowledge-graph already covers typed-node/edge structural querying, but a reader of it still learns the language-agnostic Universal AST idea and the dependency-BFS incremental update mechanism only from this note.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The claims attach to a public open-source project whose implementation can be inspected, even if the benchmark figures are self-reported.

durability.rationale: The mechanisms — universal node types unifying languages, relationship-first edges, dependency-tracked incremental updates, layered query caching — are architecture patterns that hold in twelve months, unlike the self-reported millisecond benchmarks decorating them.

actionability.rationale: It gives someone building code intelligence concrete design blueprints (node-type enum, language-adapter trait, affected-file BFS, index/cache hierarchy) rather than product-only steps.

atomicity.rationale: Everything serves one statable design — maintain the whole codebase as an incrementally-updated language-agnostic graph so structural queries are cheap — with the performance sections as supporting detail, not separate ideas.
